02-question-to-answer.html: Ingestion preserves source text and prepares document embeddings and a matching Qdrant index.
Retrieval MCP encodes the question with shared BGE, searches the index and reads prepared text.
Relevant passages return to the coordinator for a grounded response.
architecture-request-path.html: The same AI Coordinator appears at planning and completion; these are two stages, not two services.
Retrieval MCP returns source evidence. A selected model route generates the response.
PostgreSQL retains conversation content independently of inference.
01-system-architecture.html: Browser HTTP/AG-UI and MCP clients reach the Coordination Layer through their respective paths.
One AI Coordinator connects question answering, artifact review and specialist delegation.
Retrieval, models, evaluation and conversation state have separate responsibilities. Ingestion runs outside conversations.
model-routing.html: The AI Coordinator receives the task, context and constraints.
The design separates simple, general, reasoning and specialized model routes.
The same coordinator gathers results, synthesizes and checks the response.
manual-ingestion.html: Selected sources pass through conversion and deterministic preparation.
Shared BGE generates embeddings; import verifies a complete bundle into a fresh index.
The operator selects matching prepared documents and index as the retrieval release.
harness-workflows.html: A client question reaches the AI Coordinator, retrieval and model services, then returns a plain answer.
Source documents become a prepared, encoded knowledge release that is verified and activated.
Selected judges provide feedback. Synthetic Owner scoring and Real Owner approval have separate revision returns.
judge-registry.html: Role, domain and relevant source evidence inform judge definitions.
Versioned personas, rubrics, criteria, datasets and examples become prepared Harbor tasks.
The NIS Judge Registry holds reusable definitions. Select the perspectives needed for each evaluation.
artifact-review-flow.html: The AI Coordinator routes the artifact and brief separately to Harbor Hub and Hugging Face, then aggregates feedback.
Scoring recommends acceptance or revision. Below threshold, the artifact and brief return for revision and evaluation.
Qualifying work reaches the person. Approval completes review; requested changes return through revision and evaluation.
case-system.html: Client interfaces reach the direct NIS API and one Deep Agents/LangGraph execution owner.
The diagram connects model providers, Retrieval MCP, allowlisted tools and PostgreSQL.
Manual conversion, preparation, embedding and import remain separate from requests. This is the historical design record, not a rollout claim.
case-evolution.html: The recorded client path passes through the LiteLLM gateway to NIS Coordination and a selected provider.
The accepted target connects the client to NIS Coordination and a LangChain direct adapter.
The two paths are alternatives on record; the diagram does not establish a completed cutover or performance comparison.
case-request.html: The historical direct-platform candidate starts from a question and explicit task requirements.
An eligible inventory is scored using configured assumptions; no eligible route produces an explicit failure.
The bounded graph searches and reads one prepared release before returning and checkpointing a supported answer.
